[PDF p. 353] His successor Murad I crossed into Europe and rapidly dismantled the remaining Byzantine territory. [PDF p. 353] A decisive engagement at Adrianople in 1361 reduced the empire to a headless trunk. [PDF p. 353] Murad I preferred campaigning against Servians and Bulgarians rather than attempting to storm the capital. [PDF p. 353] The author notes that the strategic reasons for this hesitation remain difficult to discern. [PDF p. 353] John V subsequently became a humble vassal obliged to besiege the final Christian stronghold in Anatolia. [PDF p. 353] The author suggests that the empire had long outlived its historical justification by 1370. [PDF p. 353] Hungarian and Servian powers assumed the primary burden of defending Christendom from Ottoman expansion. [PDF p. 353]

Manuel II ascended the throne after enduring multiple domestic rebellions and relentless Ottoman pressure. [PDF p. 354] The Battle of Angora in 1402 shattered the Ottoman army and triggered a prolonged period of strife. [PDF p. 354] Manuel II skillfully navigated this chaos to temporarily recover several provincial territories. [PDF p. 354] He failed to exploit the Turkish disunity because Hungarian forces remained occupied by Hussite conflicts. [PDF p. 354] Murad II resumed hostilities and besieged Constantinople with early artillery in the year 1422. [PDF p. 354] The city walls successfully repelled the assault, and Manuel II died in 1425. [PDF p. 354] His successor John VI ruled cautiously while the capital deteriorated into poverty and ruin. [PDF p. 354] He pursued religious union with Rome in 1438 to secure vital Western military assistance. [PDF p. 354] The policy provoked violent clerical opposition and permanently alienated his own population. [PDF p. 354]

Constantine XI assumed power in 1448 under deeply divided and hostile circumstances. [PDF p. 355] Sultan Mohammed II prepared a systematic siege that began in the spring of 1453. [PDF p. 355] Heavy cannon batteried the ancient fortifications while Turkish forces relentlessly assaulted the breaches. [PDF p. 355] Genoese mercenaries provided crucial support but could not offset the overwhelming numerical disparity. [PDF p. 355] The city fell on May 29, 1453, after fierce resistance near the Gate of St. Romanus. [PDF p. 355] Constantine perished in the final assault, and the Ottoman sultan entered the great basilica of St. Sophia. [PDF p. 355] The conquest definitively terminated the longest imperial tenure in Christian history. [PDF p. 355] The source material concentrates exclusively on diplomatic and military narratives while omitting detailed economic statistics. [PDF p. 355] The text also lacks comprehensive analysis regarding the internal administration of the decaying empire. [PDF p. 355]
